analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: StatusCommandRunTests.swift (new lateLeaseRenewalStillAuthorizes, head lines 254-279) and ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests.swift (new tests at head lines 100-260, plus updated summary() call signatures at 134-140 and 262-271). No production code is in this batch, so no new attack surface is introduced here.

The tests describe a split in production behavior, and that production change is not supplied. It separates a display decision (displayedStatus / displayedProviderAuthorization) from a removal decision (currentStatus / currentProviderAuthorization). Display keeps reporting App Attest authorization while the lease is unexpired, even if the last renewal is older than snapshotMaxAge. Removal (MDM unenroll) still requires a renewal received within the 10 s window, plus matching session, machine, protocol version and reason. The tests assert that a late lease does not offer removal and instead says it needs fresh coordinator readiness. They also assert that a removal decision cannot restore a missing or expired displayed authorization. Expiry, NaN/infinity and the daemon-write-time bound (writtenAt within the window, so the lease cannot outlive a daemon that stopped writing) are covered.

These tests align with the T-053 and T-057 concerns: stale authorization must not enable destructive MDM removal, and a display-only leniency must not become a removal authorization. Display is status text only, and removal stays strict.

Questions for the integration pass, which can only be checked against the production diff:
- Whether displayedStatus checks every condition the tests assume (processMatches, coordinatorMatches, status == online, path == app_attest, finite expiresAt > now, writtenAt window).
- Whether the unenroll command uses only currentProviderAuthorization and never displayed.
- Whether summary() compares session, machine, reason and protocol version between the displayed and removal authorizations.

The tests include a print() witness line, which is harmless. No findings.
